decision: Retain production in this source PR; prioritize a spectroscopic-D0 candidate because modern evidence favors a smaller dissociation energy D0, while thermal/state selection must be explicit.

primary.inspection: Full published 15-page paper, sections 2.3/3.1/4 and current official states/PF/definition.
primary.findings: Khan model includes X/A/B/C singlets, bound/quasi-bound selection and MARVELized levels. Nuclear spin product 8. The paper explicitly notes an unexplained extra factor two in BC2016 KH and divides it for its figure.

primary.inspection: Publisher abstract inspected; original full text not acquired. Khan 2026 separately confirms adopted De.
primary.findings: Spectroscopic resonance-width analysis reports De=14772.7 +/-0.6 cm-1 and D0=14282.6 cm-1. The quoted +/-0.6 is attached to De; do not silently relabel it as a complete D0 uncertainty.

primary.inspection: Pinned numerical excerpts reused; older spectroscopic originals not reaudited.
primary.findings: BC D0=1.7708 eV agrees with the 1988 spectroscopic D0 to tabulation precision; its raw Q carries the factor-two issue. Production KH is JANAF, so no factor-two correction is applied to production.

limitations: Published PF includes noninteger rounded temperature knots. Replay uses the actual nearest knot, not an invented exact integer value; remaining small mismatch is not claimed to be fully explained by rounding.
Paper PF discussion names X/A/B while distributed states also include C. C contribution and boundary populations are quantified without discarding states or declaring completeness.
Metadata maximum 5000 K and tabulated PF through 10001 K are distinct; no global omitted-state or isotope-mixture bound is established.
followups: Build a provisional energy-only candidate using the inspected D0=14282.6 cm-1, explicitly retaining abstract-only uncertainty limits; use the full 1988 paper if a precision uncertainty claim is needed.
Reconcile Khan PF generation, MARVELization and X/A/B/C bound/quasi-bound selection, then compare Q/H/S/Cp with production and NASA thermal candidates.
